passages.text: Israel was a luxuriant vine, yielding fruit for himself. The more his fruit increased, the more he increased the altars. The better his land produced, the better he made the sacred pillars.
passages.sermon:
Israel is like a rich vine.
This vine grows many branches.
Israel produces much fruit for himself.
As Israel’s fruit increases, he builds more altars.
When Israel’s land becomes better, he makes the sacred pillars even better.
passages.original: גֶּ֤פֶן בּוֹקֵק֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל פְּרִ֖י יְשַׁוֶּה־ לּ֑וֹ כְּרֹ֣ב לְפִרְי֗וֹ הִרְבָּה֙ לַֽמִּזְבְּח֔וֹת כְּט֣וֹב לְאַרְצ֔וֹ הֵיטִ֖יבוּ מַצֵּבֽוֹת׃

passages.text: Their hearts are devious; now they must bear their guilt. The LORD will break down their altars and demolish their sacred pillars.
passages.sermon:
The people have devious hearts.
They must now bear their guilt.
The LORD will break down their altars.
The LORD will demolish their sacred pillars.
passages.original: חָלַ֥ק לִבָּ֖ם עַתָּ֣ה יֶאְשָׁ֑מוּ ה֚וּא יַעֲרֹ֣ף מִזְבְּחוֹתָ֔ם יְשֹׁדֵ֖ד מַצֵּבוֹתָֽם׃

passages.text: Surely now they will say, “We have no king, for we do not revere the LORD. What can a king do for us?”
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel do not respect the LORD.
They say, “We have no king.”
They do not fear God.
They ask, “What can a king do for us?”
passages.original: כִּ֤י עַתָּה֙ יֹֽאמְר֔וּ אֵ֥ין מֶ֖לֶךְ לָ֑נוּ כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יָרֵ֙אנוּ֙ אֶת־ יְהֹוָ֔ה וְהַמֶּ֖לֶךְ מַה־ יַּֽעֲשֶׂה־ לָּֽנוּ׃

passages.text: They speak mere words; with false oaths they make covenants. So judgment springs up like poisonous weeds in the furrows of a field.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel speak only words.
They do not speak truth.
They make promises that are false.
They make agreements with lies.
Their words have no value.
Their oaths are empty.
They make covenants that do not last.
Because of this, judgment comes quickly.
Judgment grows like poisonous weeds.
The weeds grow in the furrows of a field.
Judgment spreads everywhere among them.
passages.original: דִּבְּר֣וּ דְבָרִ֔ים אָל֥וֹת שָׁ֖וְא כָּרֹ֣ת בְּרִ֑ית וּפָרַ֤ח כָּרֹאשׁ֙ מִשְׁפָּ֔ט עַ֖ל תַּלְמֵ֥י שָׂדָֽי׃

passages.text: The people of Samaria will fear for the calf of Beth-aven. Indeed, its people will mourn with its idolatrous priests— those who rejoiced in its glory— for it has been taken from them into exile.
passages.sermon:
The people of Samaria live in the city of Samaria.
They will fear for the calf of Beth-aven.
Beth-aven is a place where people worshiped an idol shaped like a calf.
The people of Samaria will mourn for this calf.
The idolatrous priests will also mourn for the calf.
These priests once rejoiced in the calf’s glory.
The calf has been taken away from them.
The calf has gone into exile.
passages.original: לְעֶגְלוֹת֙ בֵּ֣ית אָ֔וֶן יָג֖וּרוּ שְׁכַ֣ן שֹֽׁמְר֑וֹן כִּי־ אָבַ֨ל עָלָ֜יו עַמּ֗וֹ וּכְמָרָיו֙ עָלָ֣יו יָגִ֔ילוּ עַל־ כְּבוֹד֖וֹ כִּֽי־ גָלָ֥ה מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: Yes, it will be carried to Assyria as tribute to the great king. Ephraim will be seized with shame; Israel will be ashamed of its wooden idols.
passages.sermon:
Assyria is a powerful nation.
The calf idol will be carried to Assyria.
People will give it as a gift to the great king of Assyria.
Ephraim is a tribe in Israel.
Ephraim will feel deep shame.
Israel will be ashamed.
Israel will be ashamed because of its own advice and trust in idols.
passages.original: גַּם־ אוֹתוֹ֙ לְאַשּׁ֣וּר יוּבָ֔ל מִנְחָ֖ה לְמֶ֣לֶךְ יָרֵ֑ב בָּשְׁנָה֙ אֶפְרַ֣יִם יִקָּ֔ח וְיֵב֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מֵעֲצָתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Samaria will be carried off with her king like a twig on the surface of the water.
passages.sermon:
Samaria is a city in Israel.
Samaria has a king.
Samaria and her king will be taken away.
They will be carried off together.
They will be like a twig floating on water.
The twig moves wherever the water takes it.
Samaria and her king will have no power to resist.
passages.original: נִדְמֶ֥ה שֹׁמְר֖וֹן מַלְכָּ֑הּ כְּקֶ֖צֶף עַל־ פְּנֵי־ מָֽיִם׃

passages.text: The high places of Aven will be destroyed— it is the sin of Israel; thorns and thistles will overgrow their altars. Then they will say to the mountains, “Cover us!” and to the hills, “Fall on us!”
passages.sermon:
Israel sinned at the high places of Aven.
These high places will be destroyed.
Thorns will grow on their altars.
Thistles will cover their altars.
The people will speak to the mountains.
They will say, "Cover us!"
They will speak to the hills.
They will say, "Fall on us!"
passages.original: וְנִשְׁמְד֞וּ בָּמ֣וֹת אָ֗וֶן חַטַּאת֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל ק֣וֹץ וְדַרְדַּ֔ר יַעֲלֶ֖ה עַל־ מִזְבְּחוֹתָ֑ם וְאָמְר֤וּ לֶֽהָרִים֙ כַּסּ֔וּנוּ וְלַגְּבָע֖וֹת נִפְל֥וּ עָלֵֽינוּ׃ס

passages.text: Since the days of Gibeah you have sinned, O Israel, and there you have remained. Did not the battle in Gibeah overtake the sons of iniquity?
passages.sermon:
Israel sinned in the days of Gibeah.
Israel continued in that sin.
The people did not leave their sinful ways.
A battle happened in Gibeah.
That battle overtook the sons of iniquity.
passages.original: מִימֵי֙ הַגִּבְעָ֔ה חָטָ֖אתָ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל שָׁ֣ם עָמָ֔דוּ לֹֽא־ תַשִּׂיגֵ֧ם בַּגִּבְעָ֛ה מִלְחָמָ֖ה עַל־ בְּנֵ֥י עַֽלְוָֽה׃

passages.text: I will chasten them when I please; nations will be gathered against them to put them in bondage for their double transgression.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about Israel.
God says, "I will punish Israel when I choose."
God will gather many nations against Israel.
These nations will put Israel in bondage.
Israel will suffer this because of their double sin.
passages.original: בְּאַוָּתִ֖י וְאֶסֳּרֵ֑ם וְאֻסְּפ֤וּ עֲלֵיהֶם֙ עַמִּ֔ים בְּאָסְרָ֖ם לִשְׁתֵּ֥י עֵינֹתָם׃

passages.text: Ephraim is a well-trained heifer that loves to thresh; but I will place a yoke on her fair neck. I will harness Ephraim, Judah will plow, and Jacob will break the hard ground.
passages.sermon:
Ephraim is like a well-trained young cow.
Ephraim loves to thresh grain.
I, the LORD, see that Ephraim has a strong and beautiful neck.
I will put a yoke on Ephraim’s neck.
I will make Ephraim pull the plow.
Judah will also plow the field.
Jacob will break up the hard ground.
passages.original: וְאֶפְרַ֜יִם עֶגְלָ֤ה מְלֻמָּדָה֙ אֹהַ֣בְתִּי לָד֔וּשׁ וַאֲנִ֣י עָבַ֔רְתִּי עַל־ ט֖וּב צַוָּארָ֑הּ אַרְכִּ֤יב אֶפְרַ֙יִם֙ יַחֲר֣וֹשׁ יְהוּדָ֔ה יְשַׂדֶּד־ ל֖וֹ יַעֲקֹֽב׃

passages.text: Sow for yourselves righteousness and reap the fruit of loving devotion; break up your unplowed ground. For it is time to seek the LORD until He comes and sends righteousness upon you like rain.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Israel.
God commands the people.
Sow righteousness for yourselves.
Reap the fruit of loving devotion.
Break up your unplowed ground.
It is time to seek the LORD.
Seek Him until He comes.
He will send righteousness upon you like rain.
passages.original: זִרְע֨וּ לָכֶ֤ם לִצְדָקָה֙ קִצְר֣וּ לְפִי־ חֶ֔סֶד נִ֥ירוּ לָכֶ֖ם נִ֑יר וְעֵת֙ לִדְר֣וֹשׁ אֶת־ יְהוָ֔ה עַד־ יָב֕וֹא וְיֹרֶ֥ה צֶ֖דֶק לָכֶֽם׃

passages.text: You have plowed wickedness and reaped injustice; you have eaten the fruit of lies. Because you have trusted in your own way and in the multitude of your mighty men, the roar of battle will rise against your people, so that all your fortresses will be demolished as Shalman devastated Beth-arbel in the day of battle, when mothers were dashed to pieces along with their children.
passages.sermon:
Israel has done evil.
Israel has worked wickedness.
Israel has harvested injustice.
Israel has eaten the fruit of lies.
Israel has trusted in its own way.
Israel has relied on its many warriors.
Because of this, battle will come against Israel.
A loud noise will rise among the people.
All Israel’s strongholds will be destroyed.
This destruction will be like what Shalman did to Beth-arbel in the day of battle.
In that day, mothers and children were killed together.
passages.original: חֲרַשְׁתֶּם־ רֶ֛שַׁע עַוְלָ֥תָה קְצַרְתֶּ֖ם אֲכַלְתֶּ֣ם פְּרִי־ כָ֑חַשׁ כִּֽי־ בָטַ֥חְתָּ בְדַרְכְּךָ֖ בְּרֹ֥ב גִּבּוֹרֶֽיךָ׃ וְקָ֣אם שָׁאוֹן֮ בְּעַמֶּךָ֒ וְכָל־ מִבְצָרֶ֣יךָ יוּשַּׁ֔ד כְּשֹׁ֧ד שַֽׁלְמַ֛ן בֵּ֥ית אַֽרְבֵ֖אל בְּי֣וֹם מִלְחָמָ֑ה אֵ֥ם עַל־ בָּנִ֖ים רֻטָּֽשָׁה׃

passages.text: Thus it will be done to you, O Bethel, because of your great wickedness. When the day dawns, the king of Israel will be utterly cut off.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Bethel.
Bethel has done great evil.
God will punish Bethel because of this evil.
When morning comes, God will destroy the king of Israel.
The king of Israel will be completely removed.
passages.original: כָּ֗כָה עָשָׂ֤ה לָכֶם֙ בֵּֽית־ אֵ֔ל מִפְּנֵ֖י רָעַ֣ת רָֽעַתְכֶ֑ם בַּשַּׁ֕חַר נִדְמֹ֥ה נִדְמָ֖ה מֶ֥לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
